title: Protocol #04: Primitive Stone Axe Fabrication (Flaked Stone & Kudzu)
summary: Essential percussion tool for timber felling, perimeter defense, and marrow bone crushing. Flake hard river quartzite into a bifacial cutting bit, seated into a split Y-haft and lashed with boiled kudzu cordage and hot pine pitch cement.

materials.name: Dense River Quartzite (RIVER QUARTZITE)
materials.desc: Palm-sized, fine-grained quartzite or basalt cobble. Percussion-flaked with a rounded hammerstone.

materials.name: Forked Oak Handle (HARDWOOD HANDLE)
materials.desc: 3.5cm diameter, 50cm long green oak limb featuring a natural Y-shaped fork.

materials.name: Boiled Kudzu Cordage & Pine Pitch (FIBER & PINE RESIN)
materials.desc: Lye-boiled tough twisted kudzu fibers and hot waterproofing pitch compound mixed with crushed charcoal.

steps.title: Percussion Flaking for Bifacial Bevel Edge
steps.description: Rest the core stone on an anvil stone. Strike the perimeter with a hammerstone at a 70-degree angle to detach sharp flakes, shaping a symmetric cutting bit.
steps.actionNote: > Action: Shield your eyes from flint shards. Grind the finished edge wet against sandstone to hone a durable razor bevel.

steps.title: Y-Fork Mortise Shaping & Blade Seating
steps.description: Insert the stone bit into the split oak handle fork. Slightly char the interior wood to burn away high spots and achieve a snug negative cavity fit.
steps.actionNote: > Science: A mortised stone-to-wood joint prevents rotational moment during high-velocity impacts, transferring shock directly along the grain.

steps.title: Figure-8 Lashings & Charcoal Pitch Seal
steps.description: Lash the stone and handle in tight figure-8 turns using wet kudzu cordage. Generously coat the binding with heated pine resin and charcoal dust cement.
steps.actionNote: > Caution: Wet plant fiber shrinks significantly upon drying, clamping the stone like an iron vise. Allow 30 minutes for pitch to fully cure before swinging.

fatalMistake.title: Fatal Mistake: Using dry twine without wet shrinkage tension or skipping resin cement.
fatalMistake.description: Impact force during chopping exceeds hundreds of kilograms. Without the immense clamping tension of dried shrinking fibers and pitch cement, the stone bit will detach mid-swing and strike your lower leg.
fatalMistake.consequence: Outcome: Compound tibial fracture and fatal wilderness hemorrhage.
